body.stem: Your team opens the Azure Backup workbooks in Log Analytics workspace la-backup. The tiles and grids that cover the workloads protected in the Recovery Services vault come back empty, while the same workbook returns rows for the workloads in the Backup vault over the same period. Both vaults have been sending logs to this workspace for several weeks, so ingestion lag does not explain the gap. You want the reports to populate for the Recovery Services vault. Which change should you make?

rows: Core Azure Backup Data; Addon Azure Backup Job Data; Addon Azure Backup Policy Data; Addon Azure Backup Storage Data; Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data; Azure Backup Operations
Core Azure Backup Data; Addon Azure Backup Job Data; Addon Azure Backup Policy Data; Addon Azure Backup Storage Data; Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data; Azure Backup Operations

options.text: Republish prod-rsv's rsv-diag setting so the six Azure Backup events are sent in Resource specific mode instead of Azure diagnostics mode.
Add the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event to prod-rsv's rsv-diag setting so it keeps being sent in Azure diagnostics mode.
Republish prod-bv's bv-diag setting so the six Azure Backup events are sent in Azure diagnostics mode instead of Resource specific mode.
Remove Addon Azure Backup Storage Data from prod-bv's bv-diag setting and add the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event to it in Resource specific mode.

explanation.correct: For a Recovery Services vault, the six Azure Backup events reach the Backup reports only when they are sent in Resource specific mode; when they are sent in Azure diagnostics mode, no data appears in the reports. prod-rsv currently sends those events in Azure diagnostics mode, which is exactly why its tiles and grids are empty, whereas prod-bv (a Backup vault) already uses Resource specific mode and therefore returns rows. Republishing rsv-diag with the same six events under Resource specific mode creates the dedicated per-event tables in la-backup (for example CoreAzureBackup and the Addon tables) that the workbooks query, and that is the recommended target mode for new settings.

perChoice.b: The legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event is supported only in Azure diagnostics mode, so adding it to that setting would indeed flow data, but the Log Analytics reporting solution is moving off the legacy event: it is on a deprecation path and the reports will cease to support data from it. The workbooks read the new per-event tables, so this change does not fill the empty tiles and keeps the estate on the route that is being retired.
perChoice.c: prod-bv is already returning data, and for Backup vaults all diagnostics events are sent to the resource-specific tables only, so there is nothing to migrate there. Republishing that setting to Azure diagnostics mode would put a working feed at risk and would not affect prod-rsv, which is the vault with the empty tiles.
perChoice.d: A diagnostic setting carries a single log mode, and the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event flows no data at all when it is sent in Resource specific mode, so the second half of this change cannot work. Addon Azure Backup Storage Data is also not applicable to a Backup vault, because storage consumed and frontend size already arrive through Core Azure Backup Data and Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data, so removing it changes nothing. This also targets the vault whose reports are already populating.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault that protects a group of Azure VMs, and your team reviews backup activity through the Backup Job History report in a Log Analytics workspace. On the morning of 29 March, with the time range set to the last 7 days, a colleague compares the report's job grid with the vault's own job list and points out two oddities: a job that started late on 23 March is filed under a date earlier than the day it actually completed, and the jobs that ran after midnight on 29 March do not appear in the report at all. You need to explain the report's counting behaviour to the colleague. Which statement is correct?

exhibit.text:
Backup Job History grid, Time Range = Last 7 days, viewed on 29 March
(row 3 comes from the vault's own Backup jobs blade, not from the grid)

Date shown in report | Backup item | Start time (UTC) | End time (UTC) | Outcome
23 Mar              | Daily-VM-01 | 23 Mar 23:50    | 24 Mar 00:06    | Succeeded
24 Mar              | Daily-VM-02 | 24 Mar 22:10    | 24 Mar 22:52    | Succeeded
Not listed          | Daily-VM-03 | 29 Mar 02:00    | 29 Mar 02:47    | Succeeded

options.text: A job is counted in the range in which it was triggered rather than the one in which it finished, and the report ends at the close of the last completed UTC day, so jobs triggered during 29 March are not listed yet.

A job is counted in the range in which it finished rather than the one in which it was triggered, and the report ends at the close of the last completed UTC day, so jobs triggered during 29 March are not listed yet.

A job is counted in the range in which it was triggered rather than the one in which it finished, and the report includes everything up to the moment the workbook is opened, so jobs triggered during 29 March are listed as they run.

A job is counted in the range in which it finished rather than the one in which it was triggered, and the report includes everything up to the moment the workbook is opened, so jobs triggered during 29 March are listed as they run.

explanation.correct: The report shows job details for the jobs that were triggered inside the selected time range, not for the range in which they completed, and the reports never include the current partial day: they always cover full UTC days, so on 29 March the data ends at 23:59 UTC on 28 March and jobs created on 29 March only appear when the report is viewed on 30 March. That is why the job that started at 23:50 on 23 March and ended after midnight on 24 March is filed under 23 March, and why the job that started at 02:00 on 29 March is absent.

perChoice.b: Wrong on the attribution half: job details are shown for jobs triggered in the selected range, not for the range in which they completed, so a job that started at 23:50 on 23 March and finished after midnight still belongs to 23 March. The statement about the last completed UTC day is right, but the counting rule it applies to is not.
perChoice.c: Wrong on the day-coverage half: the report never shows the current partial day; it always uses complete UTC days, which is why jobs from 29 March are missing while the report is viewed on 29 March. The trigger-time part of the statement is correct.
perChoice.d: Wrong on both halves: jobs are attributed to the range in which they were triggered, not the one in which they finished, and the report excludes the current partial day instead of including everything up to the moment the workbook is opened.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault in West Europe that sends diagnostic logs to the Log Analytics workspace la-backup-prod in East US 2. The workspace retention is set to 30 days, and the compliance team wants a 12-month trend of backup job outcomes read from the Backup Reports workbook in Log Analytics. You need that reporting period to cover the full 12 months. Which action should you take?

rows: Resource specific mode, six Azure Backup events
Backup Reports workbook in Log Analytics

options.text: Increase the retention of la-backup-prod to 365 days; the workspace can stay in East US 2 while the vault remains in West Europe, even in a different subscription.

Keep the retention of the la-backup-prod workspace at 30 days in East US 2 and add a diagnostic destination that sends the vault's logs from West Europe to a storage account in the same region and subscription as the vault, then assemble the 12-month trend by querying the archived log files.

Keep the retention of la-backup-prod at 30 days in East US 2 and enable the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event in Azure diagnostics mode so that the Backup Reports workbook shows the 12-month trend.

Increase the retention of la-backup-prod to 180 days and reconfigure the vault's diagnostic setting to Resource specific mode with the six new events so that the Backup Reports workbook covers the full 12 months.

explanation.correct: Azure Backup reports are rendered by workbooks whose Kusto queries run against the Log Analytics workspace, and data in that workspace is retained for 30 days by default, so the retention period has to be extended whenever a longer reporting horizon is required. Raising the retention on la-backup-prod to 365 days makes a full year of history queryable by the Backup Reports workbook. The location and subscription of the workspace are independent of the vault that feeds it, so a workspace in East US 2 and a vault in West Europe in different subscriptions need no relocation.

perChoice.b: Archiving the vault's diagnostic logs in a storage account is the option for keeping raw logs for custom analysis; it does not feed the Backup Reports workbook, whose widgets query the Log Analytics workspace. With the workspace still at 30 days, the workbook cannot cover 12 months. A Recovery Services vault can also only send diagnostic logs to a storage account located in its own region.
perChoice.c: The legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event is supported only in Azure diagnostics mode and is on a deprecation path, and the Log Analytics reporting solution is also ceasing support for data from it; it is kept only for existing custom queries and visualizations. Enabling it does not change the workspace's 30-day retention, so the workbook still cannot show a 12-month trend.
perChoice.d: Using Resource specific mode with the six new events is the recommended way to feed the reports, but a 180-day retention is far shorter than the requested 12-month horizon, so the workbook would still return only about six months of data.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault that protects a group of Azure VMs, and its backup logs already reach a Log Analytics workspace where the workbook tiles show job outcomes. You need the on-call rotation to be notified whenever Azure Backup raises an alert about a protected item, using a notification path that remains supported going forward. Which change should you make?

rows: Core Azure Backup Data; Addon Azure Backup Job Data; Addon Azure Backup Policy Data; Addon Azure Backup Storage Data; Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data; Azure Backup Operations

options.text: Create an Azure Monitor alert and route the fired alert through an alert processing rule and an action group that targets a logic app, webhook, or runbook.
Enable the Addon Azure Backup Alerts category in the vault's existing diagnostic setting and let the classic alerts solution notify the on-call rotation.
Enable the Addon Azure Backup Alerts category in the vault's existing diagnostic setting and pair it with an Azure Monitor action group that targets a logic app.
Create an Azure Monitor alert that queries the Addon Azure Backup Alerts table in the workspace every five minutes, without an alert processing rule or action group.

explanation.correct: The classic alerts solution has been deprecated in favour of Azure Monitor-based alerting, so the Addon Azure Backup Alerts category should not be selected for this. The supported pattern is to create an Azure Monitor alert, then use an alert processing rule to route the fired alert and an action group that invokes a logic app, webhook, or runbook to reach the on-call rotation.

perChoice.b: This depends on the classic alerts solution, which is deprecated; the Addon Azure Backup Alerts category should not be selected. Notification should come from an Azure Monitor alert combined with an alert processing rule and an action group.
perChoice.c: Selecting the deprecated Addon Azure Backup Alerts category is the part to avoid, even though an action group is attached to it. An action group alone does not replace the deprecated event; the alert should be created in Azure Monitor and passed through an alert processing rule to an action group.
perChoice.d: The query depends on data from the Addon Azure Backup Alerts category, which is deprecated and is not among the categories enabled in the vault's diagnostic setting, so the query would return no usable data. On top of that, omitting both an alert processing rule and an action group leaves no target that can notify the on-call rotation.
